definitions.explanation: A hearty miso soup made with pork and root vegetables such as daikon, carrots, burdock root, and taro. A popular comfort food, especially in autumn and winter.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}い{日|ひ}には{豚汁|とんじる}がおいしい。
examples.english: Pork miso soup is delicious on cold days.

examples.japanese: {大根|だいこん}と{人参|にんじん}をたっぷり{入|い}れた{豚汁|とんじる}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made pork miso soup with plenty of daikon and carrots.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りの{屋台|やたい}で{豚汁|とんじる}が{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}われた。
examples.english: Pork miso soup was served at the festival food stalls.

notes:
PRONUNCIATION:
{豚汁|とんじる} has two accepted readings: とんじる (more common in eastern Japan) and ぶたじる (more common in western Japan). Both are widely understood.

USAGE:
{豚汁|とんじる} is a staple of home cooking and is often served at community events, festivals, and school lunches. It is heartier than regular {味噌汁|みそしる} due to the pork and abundance of root vegetables. It is sometimes described as a meal in itself when paired with rice.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {豚汁|とんじる}を{作|つく}る: to make pork miso soup
- {豚汁|とんじる}{定食|ていしょく}: pork miso soup set meal
- {具|ぐ}だくさんの{豚汁|とんじる}: pork miso soup full of ingredients
